diagnostics.message: :module.forge_trust_validator_lambda: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.forge_trust_validator_lambda: explicit depends_on of :module.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references

`module.forge_trust_validator_lambda` already depends on `aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda` implicitly because it passes `logging_log_group = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda.name`. The explicit `depends_on = [aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda]` duplicates that already-established dependency and can be removed.

`aws_cloudwatch_event_target.forge_trust_validator_lambda` already depends on `module.forge_trust_validator_lambda` implicitly via `arn = module.forge_trust_validator_lambda.lambda_function_arn`. The explicit `depends_on = [module.forge_trust_validator_lambda]` duplicates that dependency and can be removed.

`aws_cloudwatch_event_target.forge_trust_validator_lambda` wires the EventBridge rule to the Lambda function, but nothing orders it after `aws_lambda_permission.forge_trust_validator_lambda`. Per the AWS provider docs, an EventBridge rule can only invoke the Lambda once the `aws_lambda_permission` resource-based policy exists; without it the rule's scheduled invocations fail with AccessDenied. The target currently depends only on the rule and the module, so add an explicit dependency on the permission.
